summary: Promotional credit applied to merged subaccount leading to unexpected charge on primary org invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a promotional/one-time credit intended for a legacy subaccount (sub-1234) was applied to a different subaccount (sub-9012) after an org consolidation on 2026-03-09, resulting in the primary org receiving a higher-than-expected invoice for the billing window.

Impact: Customer saw an overcharge of $2,340 on the finalized invoice for billing period 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-15. Affects financial reconciliation for their accounting team and blocks autopay until credit is explained or applied.

Environment: Production (prod-us-west). Consolidation sequence initiated via the Console org-merge flow. Postback and billing services processed events in standard pipeline.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 org consolidation performed by BrightSaas admin; 2026-03-10 customer noticed invoice discrepancy and opened ticket; 2026-03-10 initial triage by Support; 2026-03-11 follow-up with Billing Eng; 2026-03-12 provisional credit approved pending final reconciliation.

Observed: The invoice line shows a promotional credit line item labeled "WELCOME_ECO_2026" applied to Org ID: org-prod-870 and not to legacy subaccount id sub-1234. Postback audit shows the postback tag for the promo event was overwritten to "sub-9012" during an alias rewrite in the consolidation job.

Expected: Promotional credit should remain associated with the original subaccount or be explicitly re-targeted to an org-level credit and reflected on the correct invoice.

Additional context: Customer provided CSV export of invoice and org-merge audit log (attached). They are requesting either (A) reallocation of the promo credit to the original subaccount invoice and an invoice correction/credit memo, or (B) a clear explanation and confirmation that the $2,340 will be refunded/waived if allocation cannot be changed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate org consolidation via Console with alias mapping (old-sub -> new-sub) in staging mirror of production
2) Trigger promotional credit issuance flow for old-sub (same promo ID WELCOME_ECO_2026),
3) Observe postback tag transformation step in consolidation job and final event emitted to billing postback-queue
4) Reconcile billing ledger to see which invoice received the credit line item

comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged receipt of CSV and audit logs. Escalating to Billing Eng for allocation logic review.

2026-03-11 | Marco Ruiz (Billing Eng): Initial hypothesis - alias rewrite in consolidation job is mutating the postback tag before billing transformation. Captured example event and queued a replay to staging postback topic.
2026-03-11 | BrightSaas (Customer): Provided org-merge transaction id OM-2026-03-09-88 and asked for timeline for fix and interim waiver.
2026-03-12 | Marco Ruiz (Billing Eng): Applied provisional credit of $2,340 to customer account (manual line item). Pending automated reconciler fix and PR to prevent future rewrites.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Org-consolidation alias rewrite step currently rewrites 'billing_tag' field on events rather than appending an alias history, causing postback processor to attribute promo to the new subaccount.

Hypothesis B: Promo issuance flow uses first-match on subaccount id; consolidation temporarily leaves both old and new ids present in the mapping table and race causes wrong mapping during event enrichment.
Evidence: postback log and org-consolidation log show ordering where alias rewrite happened before promo-event enrichment finished. Replayed event to staging reproduced misallocation consistently.
Mitigation: Add alias_history array to postback event schema so billing reconciler can determine original target. Short-term fix implemented as a replay-and-reconcile patch (PR referenced).
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-service/pull/629 - prevents destructive rewrite of billing_tag during consolidation job.
Related runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/15782/Org+Consolidation+Runbook - added a note about promo issuance ordering and a validation step.
resolution:
Provisional credit of $2,340 applied to BrightSaas account on 2026-03-12 while engineering deployed a non-destructive alias handling fix to staging and then production. Root cause: org-consolidation job rewrote billing_tag on promo postbacks, causing promo to be attributed to the merged subaccount. Released PR to ensure consolidation appends alias_history instead of overwriting billing tags.

Follow-up actions: billing team to issue a formal credit memo (CM-2026-88) on next billing cycle; engineering to monitor reconciliation runs for two cycles; update consolidation runbook with validation step; communicate RCA to customer and confirm invoice correction once final reconciliation completes.
